documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY, received 1/12/2026
Admitted 1/6/2026, discharged 1/9/2026. Service: pulmonary and critical care.

Reason for admission: unresponsive at home following a convulsive seizure, with hypoventilation.

History: 36-year-old man with epilepsy diagnosed May 2025 on valproic acid 500 mg twice daily, reports no missed doses. His roommate heard a noise early in the morning and found him having a generalized tonic-clonic seizure that lasted about two minutes and stopped without intervention; he did not wake fully afterward and EMS was called. Prior convulsion May 2025. No alcohol, no illness, slept normally.

Arrival: T 37.0 C, BP 130/85, HR 88, RR 8, SpO2 92% on room air. GCS 13, drowsy but rousable, no focal findings.
Arterial gas on arrival: pH 7.28, PaCO2 60, HCO3 29, PaO2 70, consistent with acute respiratory acidosis from postictal hypoventilation.

Hospital course:
1. Seizure / epilepsy. Admitted to the ICU for airway watch. Placed on supplemental oxygen; respiratory drive and alertness recovered over several hours with no need for ventilatory support, and by early afternoon he was oriented with RR 16 and SpO2 97%. Valproate level on arrival 71 mcg/mL. Neurology consulted: no further seizures in hospital; level therapeutic and adherence good; recommend continuing valproic acid 500 mg twice daily unchanged with outpatient follow-up.
2. Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis. He received several liters of 0.9% saline in the first 24 hours. Morning labs 1/7: Na 142, Cl 116, HCO3 17, anion gap 9, a non-gap acidosis from the saline load. Fluids changed to a balanced crystalloid then stopped as he ate and drank. 1/8: Cl 105, HCO3 23. Resolved.

Discharge condition: stable, at baseline mental status, ambulating, tolerating diet.

Discharge diagnoses: epilepsy with breakthrough generalized tonic-clonic seizure; postictal hypoventilation with acute respiratory acidosis, resolved; hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis due to excess normal saline infusion, resolved.

Discharge medications: valproic acid 500 mg by mouth twice daily (no change).
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Instructions: no driving for six months from 1/6/2026 per state guidelines; seizure precautions; follow up with PCP within a week and with outpatient neurology.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Discharge summary received and routed. Called pt: home since Friday, tired but OK, no further seizures, taking valproic acid 2 caps twice a day. Med list reviewed, no new meds. Appt with PCP tomorrow 11:00, roommate driving.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital f/u.

Admitted 1/6 to 1/9 after a generalized seizure at home, found by his roommate, slow breathing on arrival with a high CO2 that corrected within hours in the ICU without a breathing tube. Picked up a non-gap acidosis from the IV saline that had corrected by the 8th. Level was in range, neurology made no changes.

Today he feels back to normal, a little sore in the shoulders the first two days. No events since. Says he has not missed a dose; can't think of a trigger. No alcohol.

Meds: valproic acid 500 mg BID. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted, SpO2 normal on room air. Alert, oriented, speech normal. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Neuro nonfocal, gait normal. No tongue injury this time.

A/P
1. Epilepsy, breakthrough GTC seizure on therapeutic valproate. Continue current dose per neurology; their follow-up is already booked for February.
2. Saline-related hyperchloremic acidosis, resolved in hospital. Repeat BMP today to close the loop; marking resolved on the problem list.
3. Driving: back to no driving, six months from 1/6, so not before early July.
4. Work note for last week provided.

documents.title: Labs from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your chemistry panel from yesterday is completely normal, including the chloride and bicarbonate that were off in the hospital. That issue is behind you. See you at the next visit.

documents.title: RE: Labs from yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great thanks. HR at work wants the note on letterhead, can you send it through here? Thx

documents.title: RE: Labs from yesterday
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Attached is the work note on practice letterhead covering 1/6 through 1/12. Let us know if your employer needs anything else.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up (outside)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology follow-up, visit 2/11/2026.

Interval: one breakthrough generalized tonic-clonic seizure on 1/6/2026 requiring ICU admission for postictal hypoventilation; valproate level 71 at that time, adherence reported as good. Nothing since. Diary otherwise blank since May 2025. Tolerating medication without tremor or GI effects.

Medications: valproic acid 500 mg twice daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: alert and oriented, cranial nerves intact, strength and reflexes normal and symmetric, gait normal, no tremor.

Assessment: epilepsy, one breakthrough seizure in the past 9 months on valproic acid.

Plan: continue valproic acid 500 mg twice daily. Seizure precautions; no driving until 7/6/2026. Return in 6 months or sooner with any event.

documents.title: Refill: valproic acid
documents.author: MA
documents.body: eRx renewal request, valproic acid 250 mg cap, 2 caps PO BID, #120. Neurology note 2/11 says continue same dose. Sent 90-day supply with 1 refill per PCP.

documents.title: Appointment Cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel 5/19 check-in, end-of-month deadline at work. Doing fine, no seizures. Did not want to rebook; will see PCP at fall physical.

documents.title: Driving again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi doc, it has been six months since January and no seizures. Neurology told me July 6 was the date. Just double checking it's fine to drive again.

documents.title: RE: Driving again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, that matches what neurology and I told you. With no events since January 6 you can drive. Same caution as before: if you miss medication or have any warning feeling, don't get behind the wheel.

documents.title: Refill: valproic acid
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request valproic acid 250 mg caps #120. Approved, 2 refills. Pt reminded about physical 9/29; CBC/CMP will be drawn that morning.
